The rule says no three R moves consecutively and no three D moves consecutively. In a string, a run of three consecutive R moves is precisely an occurrence of the substring RRR at three consecutive positions, because each such position contributes one R and consecutive positions correspond to consecutive moves. Likewise a run of three consecutive D moves is exactly a substring DDD. Therefore a string violates 'never take three R moves consecutively' if and only if it contains RRR, and violates the D rule if and only if it contains DDD. The no-three-consecutive constraint is thus equivalent to forbidding both substrings RRR and DDD anywhere in the move string.
